title: Scalar compatibility of normalized zero-fibre section specialization
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings, φ:A→B a unital homomorphism, and N>0 with NA=0. Let S be Noetherian with N invertible. Let g:V→S be compactifiable, separated, quasi-compact and smooth of pure relative dimension d, with a closed section s satisfying s≫g=1 and the actual finite-ring section-deformation Geometry witness [lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation]. Work in the ordinary small-etale derived categories, using derived scalar extension Q [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let κ_A and κ_B be isomorphisms of the actual Rees section families with the affine-line pullbacks of their section invariants, each normalized at one by the specified fibre mate [def-pur-noetherian-section-specialization-arrows]. Write δ_A and δ_B for their specified zero-fibre specialization arrows. Using the actual exceptional section coefficient maps q [def-pur-dnc-coefficient-section-maps], Q_S(δ_A) ≫ q_normal = q_(g,s) ≫ δ_B. No bundle integration, Tate exponent change, diagonal factor or smooth orientation is part of this statement.

proof.text: Construct the canonical normalized B-family comparison by scalar/base-change of the actual Rees coefficient maps, finite-family constancy, and shifted-line rigidity; restricting its conjugation identity to the zero fibre gives the specialization square.
The supplied B-comparison is the unique normalized comparison. Replace the canonical comparison by the supplied one in the square.
